properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued October 10 at 4:33AM EDT until October 10 at 5:30AM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
SMWTBW

The National Weather Service in Ruskin has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Coastal waters from Englewood to Tarpon Springs FL out 20 NM...
Coastal waters from Tarpon Springs to Suwannee River FL out 20
NM...
Waters from Englewood to Tarpon Springs FL out 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Tarpon Springs to Suwannee River FL out 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 530 AM EDT.

* At 433 AM EDT, strong thunderstorms were located along a line
extending from 7 nm west of Bayport to 30 nm west of Indian Rocks
Beach, moving northeast at 35 knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Expect wind gusts in excess of 34 knots, suddenly higher
waves, frequent lightning, and heavy downpours. Make sure
all on board are wearing life jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Ozello, Crystal River, Indian Shores, Clearwater Beach, Bayport,
Madeira Beach Reef, Tarpon Springs, Belleair Beach, Indian Rocks
Beach, Dunedin, Hernando Beach, Clearwater Pass, Port Richey,
Anclote Key, Indian Shore Reef, Pass-A-Grille Reef, Belleair
Shores, Aripeka, Honeymoon Island, and Caladesi Island.
properties.instruction: Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

properties.title: Special Marine Warning issued October 10 at 3:45AM EDT until October 10 at 4:45AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
SMWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Waters from Altamaha Sound GA to Fernandina Beach FL from 20 to 60
NM...

* Until 445 AM EDT.

* At 345 AM EDT, a strong thunderstorm was located 21 nm southeast of
Tug Rio Caroni, or 21 nm south of R2 Tower, moving north at 50
knots.

HAZARD...Wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Small craft could be damaged in briefly higher winds and
suddenly higher waves.

* The strong thunderstorm will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately. If your vessel is caught offshore, immediately secure
for heavy weather. Ensure all crew members are wearing USCG approved
Type I life jackets and nonessential crew are below decks. Deploy
jack lines and harnesses if available. Check life saving equipment,
including batteries on handheld radios, for readiness.
properties.area: Waters from Altamaha Sound GA to Fernandina Beach FL from 20 to 60 NM

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 10 at 3:35AM EDT until October 10 at 12:45PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Coffee County in southeastern Alabama...
Western Dale County in southeastern Alabama...
Geneva County in southeastern Alabama...

* WHEN...Until 1145 AM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to
excess runoff from earlier rainfall. It will take several hours for
all the water from these storms to work through local drainage
systems in urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 232 AM CDT, Extremely heavy rain on Friday night due to
Hurricane Isaias brought 5 to 12 inches of rain to the warned
area. Heavy rain has ended, but small streams, creeks and rivers
will continue to rise and flood for at least several more hours
as water moves downhill and downstream.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Daleville, Elba, Enterprise, Fort Rucker, Geneva, Ozark, Level
Plains, Samson, New Brockton, Ariton, Lee, Clayhatchee, Kinston,
Coffee Springs, Enterprise Municipal A/P, Turner Crossroads,
Battens Crossroads, Lucile and Shell Army Field.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

In hilly terrain there are hundreds of low water crossings which are
potentially dangerous in heavy rain. Do not attempt to cross flooded
roads. Find an alternate route.
properties.area: Coffee, AL; Dale, AL; Geneva, AL

* WHERE...Pea River at Elba (US 84).

* WHEN...From this evening to Sunday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 30.0 feet, Minor flooding will affect farmland along
the Pea River near Elba.

feet on 04/06/1937.

properties.title: Tropical Storm Warning issued October 10 at 2:07AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
* LOCATIONS AFFECTED
- Dawson

* WIND
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Below tropical storm force wind
- Peak Wind Forecast: 10-20 mph with gusts to 40 mph

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for wind 39
to 57 mph
- The wind threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Plan for hazardous wind of equivalent tropical storm
force.
- PREPARE: Efforts to protect property should now be
underway. Prepare for limited wind damage.
- ACT: Act now to complete preparations before the wind
becomes hazardous.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Limited
- Damage to porches, awnings, carports, sheds, and unanchored
mobile homes. Unsecured lightweight objects blown about.
- Many large tree limbs broken off. A few trees snapped or
uprooted, but with greater numbers in places where trees
are shallow rooted. Some fences and roadway signs blown
over.
- A few roads impassable from debris, particularly within
urban or heavily wooded places. Hazardous driving
conditions on bridges and other elevated roadways.
- Scattered power and communications outages.

* FLOODING RAIN
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST: Flood Watch is in effect
- Peak Rainfall Amounts: Additional around 1 inch

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for major
flooding rain
- The flooding rain threat has remained nearly steady from
the previous assessment.
- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for
major flooding from heavy rain. Evacuations and rescues are
likely.
- PREPARE: Strongly consider protective actions, especially
if you are in an area vulnerable to flooding.
- ACT: Heed any flood watches and warnings. Failure to take
action will likely result in serious injury or loss of life.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Extensive
- Major rainfall flooding may prompt many evacuations and
rescues.
- Rivers and tributaries may rapidly overflow their banks in
multiple places. Small streams, creeks, and ditches may
become dangerous rivers. Flood control systems and barriers
may become stressed.
- Flood waters can enter many structures within multiple
communities, some structures becoming uninhabitable or
washed away. Many places where flood waters may cover
escape routes. Streets and parking lots become rivers of
moving water with underpasses submerged. Driving conditions
become dangerous. Many road and bridge closures with some
weakened or washed out.

* TORNADO
- LATEST LOCAL FORECAST:
- Situation is favorable for tornadoes

- THREAT TO LIFE AND PROPERTY THAT INCLUDES TYPICAL FORECAST
UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for several
tornadoes
- The tornado threat has remained nearly steady from the
previous assessment.
- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for
several tornadoes with a few possibly intense having larger
damage paths.
- PREPARE: Those living in manufactured homes or on boats
should prepare to relocate to safe shelter before hazardous
weather arrives.
- ACT: Listen for tornado watches and warnings. If a tornado
warning is issued, be ready to shelter quickly.

- POTENTIAL IMPACTS: Significant
- The occurrence of scattered tornadoes can hinder the
execution of emergency plans during tropical events.
- Several places may experience tornado damage with a few
spots of considerable damage, power loss, and
communications failures.
- Locations could realize roofs torn off frame houses, mobile
homes demolished, boxcars overturned, large trees snapped
or uprooted, vehicles tumbled, and small boats tossed
about. Dangerous projectiles can add to the toll.

* FOR MORE INFORMATION:
- Local Weather Conditions and Forecasts: NWS Tallahassee
- https://www.weather.gov/tallahassee
- Information from the Georgia Emergency Management Agency
- https://ready.ga.gov

properties.title: Flash Flood Warning issued October 10 at 2:05AM EDT until October 10 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Peachtree City GA
properties.description:
FFWFFC

The National Weather Service in Peachtree City has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Southwestern Chattahoochee County in west central Georgia...
Southwestern Harris County in west central Georgia...
Muscogee County in west central Georgia...

* Until 800 AM EDT.

* At 205 AM EDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain across the warned
area. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen. The expected
rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour. Additional rainfall
amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the warned area. Flash
flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by heavy rainfall.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Columbus, Bibb City, Fort Benning/Lawson Army Air Fld, Kenwood,
Edgewood, Columbus Metropolitan Airport, Highland Park, Vista
Terrace, Saint Marys Hills, Laurel Hills, Avondale, Rose Hill, Flat
Rock, Benning Park, Benning Hills, Green Island Hills, Sand Hill,
Carter Acres, Custer Road Terrace and Fortson.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

properties.title: Flood Advisory issued October 10 at 12:13AM EDT until October 12 at 2:00PM EDT by NWS Greenville-Spartanburg SC
properties.description:
...The Flood Advisory continues for the following rivers in North
Carolina...

French Broad River Near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W Fletcher
affecting Buncombe and Henderson Counties.

.Heavy rainfall from the remnants of Hurricane Isaias will result in
excessive runoff and significant rises on streams within the upper
French Broad River watershed.  Rainfall will develop overnight
tonight, intensify during the day on Saturday, and maintain intensity
through early Sunday morning before tapering off by Sunday
mid-morning.  Storm-total rainfall of 4-8 inches is expected, with
isolated 8-10 inches possible, across the upper French Broad River
watershed, generally upstream of Etowah.  The highest totals will
occur along the Tanassee and Pisgah ridges, with lesser amounts
within the upper French Broad River valley.  Additionally, 4-6 inches
of rainfall are expected within the Mud Creek watershed in Henderson
County, which is a primary tributary of the French Broad River above
Fletcher.  While there continues to be some uncertainty regarding the
exact location, timing, and amounts of the heaviest rainfall, there
is enough confidence in the current forecast that out-of-bank
conditions are likely for the upper French Broad River.  Therefore, a
River Flood Advisory has been issued for the reach near Fletcher,
with a crest above Action Stage expected around Sunday afternoon.  A
rise above Action Stage will result in nuisance, relatively shallow
flooding of low-lying areas adjacent to the French Broad River,
including farmland, woodlands, low-lying secondary roads, greenways,
parks, and other flood-prone locations.  Additional River Flood
Advisories are possible Saturday, especially for the French Broad
River reach near Blantyre.

More significant rises along the French Broad River are possible, and
those with interests along the river are encouraged to stay weather
aware and up-to-date on the latest stream levels and forecasts at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/GSP.  Current reasonable worst-case
scenarios are posted in the ADDITIONAL DETAILS sections below.
Forecast crests above Minor Flood Stage may result in the River Flood
Advisories being upgraded to River Flood Warnings.

* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues.

* WHERE...French Broad River near at Old Fanning Bridge Rd, 3 W
Fletcher.

* WHEN...Until Monday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...At 10.0 feet, Action/Advisory Stage.  The French Broad
River has exceeded bankfull at the gauge site.  Isolated farmland
flooding is beginning across the French Broad River Valley from
Etowah downstream to Avery Creek upstream of the gauge site.

* At 11.5 feet, Action Stage Flooding continues.  Butler Bridge Rd.
is inundated with up to 6 inches of floodwaters from the French
Broad River, forcing road closure.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 10:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 3.6 feet and steady.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 10.6 feet
early Sunday afternoon.  A crest closer to 12 feet is possible.
A reasonable worst-case crest above Minor Flood Stage below 15
feet cannot be ruled out.
- Action/Advisory Stage is 10.0 feet.
- Minor Flood Stage is 13.0 feet.

foundations. Several places may experience expanded areas

UNCERTAINTY IN TRACK, SIZE AND INTENSITY: Potential for several

previous assessment.
- PLAN: Emergency plans should include the potential for
several tornadoes with a few possibly intense having larger
damage paths.

weather arrives.

communications failures.

homes demolished, boxcars overturned, large trees snapped
or uprooted, vehicles tumbled, and small boats tossed
about. Dangerous projectiles can add to the toll.

Jefferson, Orange and Jasper Counties.

Saltwater Barrier...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Neches River at Neches River Saltwater Barrier.

* WHEN...From this evening to Monday morning.

* IMPACTS...At 5.0 feet, Water is about two feet over portions of
Four Oaks Ranch Road.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:15 PM CDT Friday the stage was 4.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 9:15 PM CDT Friday was 4.0 feet.

morning and continue falling to 3.9 feet Wednesday evening.
- Flood stage is 4.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

through flooded areas.

tornadoes

assessment.

hazardous weather arrives.

quickly.

power and communications disruptions.

chimneys toppled, mobile and manufactured homes pushed off
foundations or overturned, downed trees, and moving
vehicles blown off roads.

properties.title: Flood Warning issued October 9 at 8:46PM EDT by NWS Tampa Bay Ruskin FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Florida...

Cypress Creek At SR 54 Worthington Gardens affecting Pasco County.

Anclote River At Elfers at Little Road affecting Pasco County.

...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Florida...

Little Manatee River At Wimauma at US 301 affecting Hillsborough
County.

Manatee River Near Myakka Head at SR 64 affecting Manatee County.

Withlacoochee At US 41 Dunnellon affecting Marion, Levy and Citrus
Counties.

.Due to recent heavy rainfall, water levels on Anclote River and
Manatee River are forecast to remain at flood stage and begin to fall
Saturday. Water levels on the Cypress Creek and Little Manatee River
are expected to continue rising and reach Flood Stage during the
weekend or early in the week.

Elevated water levels continue on the Withlacoochee River at
Dunnellon due to a combination of excessive hydrilla growth along a
4.5 mile stretch of river between U.S. 41 and Lake Rousseau, and
recent heavy rainfall. Water levels are expected to hold steady
before slowly decreasing over the next several days. However, the
river is forecast to remain in flood stage.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and is forecast to continue.

* WHERE...Withlacoochee at US 41 Dunnellon.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 28.2 feet, Docks and boat ramps flood along the river
in Citrus and Marion counties.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:45 PM EDT Friday the stage was 28.3 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 28.2 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:45 PM EDT Friday was 28.5 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 28.3 feet
just after midnight tonight.
- Flood stage is 28.2 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 28.3
feet on 10/05/1965.
- https://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

properties.description:

.The St Johns River at Astor has reached Moderate Flood Stage due to
northeast winds and repeated rounds of heavy rainfall across the
basin. River levels are then forecast to remain just above Moderate
Flood Stage through this weekend and into early next week.

For the St. Johns River...including Astor...Moderate flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Moderate flooding is occurring and is forecast.

* WHERE...St Johns River near Astor.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 3.0 feet, Water approaches or may enter lowest homes
on or near Wildhog Road and nearby canals. Flooding reaches the
parking lot of the Juno Trail Apartments. Flooding on portions of
Alligator Road and Holiday Road. Lowest lying yards along Blue
Creek are flooded. Roads at Astor Landing Campground and Lake
Dexter Boat Ramp begin to flood. Water enters lower homes closest
to the river on McPherson Lane.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 PM EDT Friday the stage was 3.1 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 2.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 7:30 PM EDT Friday was 3.1 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 3.2 feet
tomorrow morning.
- Flood stage is 2.3 feet.
